analysis.title: US TMT quick hits - 29 Oct 2026
key_insights: NDX fell about 170 bps on 29 Oct on a Tech 'digestion' day, with rates, oil, USD and VIX all largely benign. Large-cap Tech drawdowns of 10-15% in GOOG, NOW and FTNT drove the move.
Semis traded two ways. The note says there was no capex worry, and the debate is the path from here after the sharp rally earlier in the week.
Internet names moved on the DASH/CART acquisition, EBAY and ETSY beats, and NFLX and SPOT fading after their prints.

Client conversations centered on the volume of newsflow and stock volatility investors must absorb in a short window. Leadership is hard to find because Software and Security are stalling, Mag 7 is described as two steps forward and one back, and Semis/AI has become 'finicky'.

Evening prints clients asked about: AMZN (Retail expectations, height of the AWS bar), INTC (DCAI momentum vs PCs, 2027 framing), PINS (3Q growth vs +13-15% y/y guide), RBLX (4Q bookings guide given GTA 6 unknowns), RDDT (US MAU trends in 3Q, licensing updates), SNDK (growth algorithm given LTAs and capital returns), TWLO (organic growth into 2027 with Voice and Agentic categories).

Post-print follow-up questions: FFIV (will investors return), NXPI (cheap enough to work), STX (HDDs vs DRAM vs NAND), EMS/Connectors preference (APH, FLEX, TTMI), EBAY/ETSY (is e-commerce inflecting or peaking).

MSFT faded with no clear reason. Cited factors were NDX down 170 bps, Software down 4%, debate on customer diversification (Orchestration story) and durability of M365 momentum (CoPilot seats, consumption uplift). The desk sees natural digestion, not a thesis change, as investors manage large-cap Tech risk into November (geopolitics, US midterms).

NOW fell 25% on investor frustration at the lack of tangible AI uplift exiting 4Q, despite a $1.7bn AI ACV figure. The desk calls it a 'show-me' story ahead of CY27 guidance next quarter. GIR sees normalized 4Q cRPO closer to 19-19.25% vs the 18.5% y/y exit-rate guide. Bulls cite ~19x CY28 non-GAAP EPS for large-cap SaaS growth.

CTSH is the latest IT Services company to cite spending headwinds after INFY's recent cut. Bookings fell 7% y/y, and management said macro uncertainty hit healthcare and consumer-facing sectors more than assumed.

Cognizant reported over 8,500 AI engagements in the quarter vs 8,000 in 1Q26, with AI assisting over 50% of software development. It sees agentic BPO expanding the addressable market from about $1tn in systems integration toward $5-6tn in enterprise operations.

E-commerce AI tailwind: ETSY estimates personalization improvements contributed about 2 percentage points to annualized y/y GMS growth, and EBAY said AI is meaningfully contributing to marketplace growth via listing and cataloging (Magical Listing).
NDX is described as 'running hard to stand still' since at least mid-May.

CTSH: bookings down 7% y/y in the reported quarter. Over 8,500 AI engagements in the quarter vs 8,000 in 1Q26.
ETSY: reported this week. Management estimates personalization improvements contributed about 2 percentage points to annualized y/y GMS growth.
EBAY: reported this week with a beat. Management said AI is meaningfully contributing to marketplace growth.
Reporting after the close 29 Oct: AMZN, COIN, COUR, DLR, DXC, GDDY, INGM, INTC, MPWR, MTZ, PINS, RBLX, RDDT, REAL, RIVN, SBUX, SNDK, TWLO. PINS 3Q growth is compared with a guide of +13-15% y/y.
